summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney transplant, coronary artery disease, prior pulmonary embolism, and heart failure presented with sudden-onset substernal chest pressure identical to her prior NSTEMI, which worsened with deep inspiration but was not associated with shortness of breath, fever, or cough. Initial evaluation revealed normal troponins, no ischemic EKG changes, and a normal chest X-ray. A V/Q scan ruled out pulmonary embolism, and an echocardiogram showed stable left ventricular function without pericardial effusion. The chest pain was attributed to post-viral pericarditis following a recent parainfluenza infection. She was started on a prednisone taper, with significant improvement in symptoms. Her amlodipine was held due to well-controlled blood pressure, and zolpidem was replaced with trazodone for insomnia. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans for outpatient follow-up and lab monitoring.
problems: Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
Personal history of other malignant neoplasm of skin
Family history of ischemic heart disease and other diseases of the circulatory system
